questions.q: What is the correct ground state electronic configuration of Chromium (Cr, atomic number 24)?
questions.qPa: ਕ੍ਰੋਮੀਅਮ (Cr, ਪਰਮਾਣੂ ਸੰਖਿਆ 24) ਦੀ ਸਹੀ ਇਲੈਕਟ੍ਰਾਨਿਕ ਸੰਰਚਨਾ ਕੀ ਹੈ?
questions.explanation: Chromium is an exception to the Aufbau principle. One 4s electron is transferred to the 3d orbital to achieve the extra stability of a half-filled d-subshell (3d5).

questions.q: Which rule states that pairing of electrons in the orbitals belonging to the same subshell does not take place until each orbital is singly occupied?
questions.explanation: Hund's Rule states that for degenerate orbitals, electrons fill them singly first, with parallel spins, before pairing begins.

questions.q: What is the electronic configuration of the Cu²⁺ ion? (Cu atomic number = 29)
questions.explanation: The neutral Cu atom is [Ar] 4s¹ 3d¹⁰. To form Cu²⁺, two electrons are removed. The first electron is removed from the highest principal quantum number (4s), and the second from the 3d. This leaves [Ar] 3d⁹.

questions.q: According to the (n+l) rule, which orbital will be filled first: 4f or 5d?
questions.explanation: For 4f, n=4 and l=3, so (n+l) = 7. For 5d, n=5 and l=2, so (n+l) = 7. Since both have the same (n+l) value, the orbital with the lower 'n' value (4f) is filled first.
